notes: Now reads at the shipping camera, which was the whole purpose of this iteration. Grid raised from 24/20 to a uniform 30 sectors and pit depths raised (crater 0.062->0.075, medium 0.046->0.058, small 0.030->0.038, tiny 0.018->0.022), putting the crater wall at about 32 degrees tangentially and 40 degrees radially instead of 22/35. All 22 pits now place on the top disk (was 20 of 22) with every size class meeting quota, verified offline by replaying the builder PRNG in check_pores.py before rendering. At azimuth 0 roughly 12-15 pits are individually countable as concave faceted marks; from top and from 90/180/270 the full field reads with a clean outer margin and no trenching. Honestly just over threshold rather than comfortably: the reference's pits still have harder octagonal rims than a one-cell grid dip can produce.

Faceting is baked as split vertices (lib.facet), so it survives the runtime's MeshLambertMaterial swap. Crisp on the rim at every azimuth. The denser face grid also improved top-face faceting over the previous pass, since the pits now break up what were near-coplanar ring triangles.
